subject: Networking preflight for hosting model selection — peering vs PrivateLink and allowlist needs
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@quantifydata.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@quantifydata.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Networking preflight for hosting model selection — peering vs PrivateLink and allowlist needs

Hi Sam / Priya —

Thanks again for the time earlier today. Quick recap and a short list of networking items we need to qualify the Private deployment path (VPC peering vs PrivateLink) so engineering can size the Dedicated vs Private VPC recommendation.

Key takeaways from the call: Quantify Data is leaning toward a private connection (you mentioned security and egress controls are priorities) but wants options that minimize cross-account networking work. You also flagged procurement timing and a static egress requirement for outbound traffic to third-party vendors.

Action items / info we need from you to proceed:  
- Preferred connectivity: do you have a firm preference for VPC peering, AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoints), or using a Transit Gateway? If undecided, say so and we can propose pros/cons.
- CIDR ranges/subnets available for peering and whether you require overlapping-check validation.
- Any existing NAT/static egress gateway requirement (we often provide a fixed egress IP range on Private deployments but need to know enforcement details).
- Firewall/allowlist rules: if you prefer allowlisting Redwood egress IPs, we'll attach our current egress list. If you require an ingress-only model (PrivateLink), let us know which accounts/regions to configure.
- Certificate/MTLS requirements and any proxy in front of your VPC (client IP translation matters).
- Contact for your network engineer to do the technical walk-through (name + email + preferred timezone).

Attached: redwood-network-reqs-v1.pdf — quick checklist and our typical config options (peering vs privatLink vs transit).

Proposed next step: 30–45m technical sync (solutions + network engineer) to run through the checklist. I can coordinate —suggested windows next week: Tue/Wed 10–12 PT.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0199

----
Attachment: redwood-network-reqs-v1.pdf (12KB stub)
From: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@quantifydata.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@quantifydata.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Networking preflight for hosting model selection — peering vs PrivateLink and allowlist needs

Ben —

Appreciate the clear recap. We're generally inclined toward VPC peering because our security team prefers no interface endpoints to manage, but we want to validate that it won't complicate routing or add additional cross-account approvals. A couple of quick answers:  

- Preferred connectivity: initial preference = VPC peering, fallback = PrivateLink if peering requires too much cross-account IAM work.
- CIDR / subnets: our primary VPC is 10.48.0.0/16 with application subnets 10.48.16.0/20 and 10.48.32.0/20. We will confirm if you need specific subnet ranges for HA testing.
- NAT/static egress: yes — we require static egress IPs for vendors. Can you provide a list of egress IPs that Redwood would use so we can allowlist?
- MTLS / certs: our security team prefers mutual TLS for control plane APIs. We can provide the CA bundle if required.
- Proxy: we do have corp outbound proxy for some subnets — will confirm which subnets are behind the proxy.

I attached our network inventory and procurement timeline so you can see gating items. Our network engineer Alex Moore will own the config; looping him in here — alex.moore@quantifydata.com. Alex, are you available for a sync Tuesday 10–11 PT?

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Jenkins
Head of Product, Quantify Data
sam.jenkins@quantifydata.com | +1 617 555 0201

----
Attachments: qd-network-inventory.xlsx (spreadsheet stub), procurement-timeline.pdf (3-page stub)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@quantifydata.com>, Alex Moore <alex.moore@quantifydata.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 02 Jul 2026 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Networking preflight for hosting model selection — peering vs PrivateLink and allowlist needs

Sam — perfect, thanks for the details and the attachments. Alex — great to meet you by email. I copied Karikth (solutions) and Marissa (customer success) so you have the right folks on the sync.

Quick notes before the call:  
- We can support both VPC peering and PrivateLink from the Redwood Private control plane. Peering tends to be simpler for high-throughput inference (less per-request handshakes) whereas PrivateLink reduces cross-account route changes but requires interface endpoints in your account. We will outline tradeoffs in the tech sync.
- Regarding static egress: Redwood can provision a stable egress IP block for Private deployments. We'll share the exact CSV of egress addresses (attached as redwood-egress-ip-list.csv) — confirm whether you need a /24 or specific single IPs.
- MTLS: Redwood's control plane supports client cert verification for restricted endpoints; for model traffic we typically rely on TLS 1.2+ and can support mTLS for the control plane. Please flag exact endpoints you want mTLS enforced on.

Proposed tech sync: Tue Jul 7, 10:00–10:45 PT — 30–45m to walk the checklist and capture route table/NAT requirements. If that works for you Alex, I’ll send a calendar invite and a shared drive doc to collect actions.

Action items I’ll own after the sync: populate a mutual action plan with 1) peering steps, 2) PrivateLink steps, 3) required firewall rules, 4) expected timeline to PROD.

Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0199

----
Attachment: redwood-egress-ip-list.csv (IP list stub)
From: Alex Moore <alex.moore@quantifydata.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@quantifydata.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@quantifydata.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Jul 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Networking preflight for hosting model selection — peering vs PrivateLink and allowlist needs

Ben / Sam —

Thanks — quick technical notes from my side before we lock the sync:  

- We can do VPC peering but need confirmation that there will be no overlapping CIDRs (we already confirmed ours). We will prefer peering for performance.
- Static egress: critical — our security team will only approve outbound connections to vendors with an allowlist of static IPs. We need Redwood to provide either: (A) a set of stable IPs (preferred), or (B) guidance on deploying a NAT instance in our VPC that guarantees a single egress IP visible to vendors.
- Ports/protocols: we only allow 443 outbound, and require SNI preserved through any proxy.
- Proxy: several of our app subnets route through a corporate outbound proxy — we'll identify which ones will be used for Redwood traffic. If we peer directly and avoid the proxy, we need to know whether client IPs are preserved for logging.

Availability: Tue Jul 7 10:00–10:45 PT works for me. Send calendar invite and a shared doc to collect checklist items.

Regards,
Alex Moore
Network Engineer, Quantify Data
alex.moore@quantifydata.com | +1 617 555 0333
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Moore <alex.moore@quantifydata.com>, Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@quantifydata.com>

Date: Sun, 05 Jul 2026 10:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Networking preflight for hosting model selection — peering vs PrivateLink and allowlist needs

Alex / Sam —

Great — invite sent for Tue Jul 7 10:00–10:45 PT. Link to shared doc: https://redwoodai.sharepoint.com/sites/Quantify-Data/Shared%20Documents/Networking-Checklist (I’ll populate the peering vs PrivateLink pros/cons before the call).

Pre-call homework for Alex / network team (so we can use the 45m effectively):  
1) Confirm which subnets (from the spreadsheet) will be used for Redwood traffic and whether they sit behind the corporate proxy.
2) Confirm whether you need a CIDR-level allowlist or a single/narrow set of egress IPs (and if the latter, whether a /32 per endpoint is required).
3) If you prefer PrivateLink, confirm which AWS account/region we should target for interface endpoints.

I'll bring a short technical playbook and our egress IP list (CSV) to the call and Karhtik will be on the call to capture the configuration steps. After the call we'll produce a mutual action plan with tasks, owners, and dates (procurement gating included).

Thanks — talk soon.
Ben
